Shanghai/Ningbo.waitLabel: SHA 8-9.5 days · NGB 5-6 days before shutdown (SEKO, 26 Aug)
Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Both halves of the pair are shutting down for Saudel. Ningbo-Zhoushan is under Ningbo MSA Level III emergency response: empty gate-in and pick-up stopped 26 Aug 16:00 HKT and laden gate-in and pick-up stopped 26 Aug 20:00 HKT across Beilun 1-3, Daxie, Meishan/MSICT, Yongzhou and Zhensi, with resumption to be announced after post-storm inspections. Shanghai began mandatory port clearance at Yangshan 26 Aug 18:00 HKT and at Waigaoqiao 27 Aug 00:01 HKT, no new berthing windows granted, and SIPG shuts Yangshan empty gates 27 Aug 04:00 and laden gates 27 Aug 06:00 HKT. Waits going into the shutdown were 9.5 days at WGQ5, 9 at WGQ2 and 8 at Yangshan 1-2, with Ningbo at 5-6 days, Meishan yard at 100 percent and over 139 boxships already in the outer anchorages. Landfall is forecast between central-southern Zhejiang and northern Fujian overnight 27-28 August.
Shanghai/Ningbo.source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 26 Aug 2026 17:30 HKT; Toll Global Forwarding advisory, 26 Aug 2026; JMA TC2621 specifications, 27 Aug 2026 06:45 JST

Xiamen.note: Container terminals are still working. Fujian gateways are on typhoon preparations — vessel tie-downs and anchorage dispersals ahead of Saudel's outer squall line — and coastal and island ferries are halted, but Toll's local team reported no impact to Xiamen port operations as of 26 August. Saudel's closest forecast approach is 332 km at 45 hours, by which point JMA has it decaying to a depression inland over Fujian, so the risk here is squall-line and rainfall disruption rather than a direct hit.
Xiamen.source: Toll Global Forwarding advisory, 26 Aug 2026; SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 26 Aug 2026; JMA TC2621 specifications, 27 Aug 2026 06:45 JST

remarks: Shanghai/Ningbo has gone from recovering to fully suspended in one run. This is the second shutdown of the month for the pair and it lands on top of a Dolphin backlog that never cleared, so the 8-9.5 day Shanghai waits are the starting point, not the peak.

Linerlytica has not published a congestion snapshot since 23 August, so the queue figures on this page are four days old and predate the Saudel clearance. Expect the anchorage numbers to jump once the feed catches up.

Haiphong and Shenzhen (Yantian) have been dropped. Narra has weakened to a depression over the Leizhou Peninsula and is tracking east-northeast away from Vietnam; SEKO now reports Haiphong, Cat Lai and Cai Mep operating normally at 0.5-1 day, and both SEKO and Toll expect only peripheral rainfall in Guangdong. Yantian's 5-6 day mega-vessel waits are ordinary congestion, not weather.
MSC has still issued no typhoon advisory despite mandatory port clearance at Shanghai and Ningbo, which is worth noting if you are relying on carrier notices rather than terminal bulletins.
